objects.original: The probabilities of one fixed final event under a finite chain of adjacent hybrids, together with per-slot error budgets.
objects.reconstructed: Arbitrary real sequences a and delta; the source instance takes a(i) to be the probability of the same event under hybrid i.
objects.evidence: The declaration uses real sequences rather than inventing a total-variation object. The lesson explicitly specifies one fixed event throughout the chain before any later supremum over events.

domains.original: A deterministic finite number of capped hybrid transitions.
domains.reconstructed: A natural number n and real values at indices zero through n, with error budgets used only at indices below n.
domains.evidence: Finset.range n contains exactly zero through n-1. The general real domain contains event probabilities as a specialization; no boundedness by one is needed by the triangle inequality. There is no random or infinite stopping claim.

quantifiers.original: For each fixed event and each adjacent hybrid pair in the finite chain, a budget controls the discrepancy, implying an endpoint bound.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For every a, delta and n, if every i<n satisfies abs(a(i+1)-a(i))<=delta(i), then the endpoint inequality holds.
quantifiers.evidence: The formal premise covers precisely all n adjacent differences. Values of delta outside the range are irrelevant. The zero case is the empty telescope and gives zero<=zero, so no positive-length assumption is missing.

assumptions.original: A supplied adjacent bound for each step of a finite hybrid chain.
assumptions.reconstructed: Only hstep: for every i<n, the adjacent absolute difference is bounded by delta(i).
assumptions.evidence: Each used delta(i) is automatically nonnegative because it bounds an absolute value. The theorem does not assume or prove that the particular source hybrid construction supplies hstep; that is an input.

conclusion.original: The endpoint event discrepancy is at most the sum of all per-slot budgets.
conclusion.reconstructed: abs(a(n)-a(0)) <= sum over i in range n of delta(i).
conclusion.evidence: The proof inserts a(n) in the successor endpoint difference, applies abs_sub_le, combines hstep with the restricted induction hypothesis and uses sum_range_succ. Source one-based call indexing is obtained by the harmless reindexing t=i+1.

scopes.original: Only the finite triangle telescope after adjacent-hybrid estimates; not the per-slot construction or capped-versus-uncapped comparison.
scopes.reconstructed: A real-sequence inequality bound only to finite-adjacent-telescope.
scopes.evidence: The binding supports exactly finite-adjacent-telescope. The lesson does not claim the adjacent estimates have been proved for an algorithm. No dummy-history construction, delta_t identification, cap error, infinite-call extension or complexity result occurs in the conclusion.

constant_dependencies.original: Every adjacent budget is counted once, with unit coefficient; the cap error is a separate later term.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: Exactly the finite sum of delta(i) for i<n, each appearing once and without any additive term.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The successor proof appends only delta(n). Neither a factor depending on n nor epsilon_cap appears; the empty sum and final index are correct.

deltas.description: The formal telescope works for arbitrary real sequences, not just event probabilities. Its source instance uses a(i)=P_i(T) for one fixed event T; the extra generality does not change the adjacent-bound argument.

Formal indices zero through n-1 correspond to source call slots one through n. The result remains an eventwise finite telescope and does not itself take the total-variation supremum or add the cap-comparison error.
